# Ultra Trail Larre®

> Non-stop 226.9 km ultra-trail with 4,644 m of positive elevation gain, run in a single self-supported, zero-waste stage across the four Álavas (Basque Country). Limited to 300 runners. 1st Edition in autumn 2027, starting at 16:00 from Parque de la Florida, Vitoria-Gasteiz.

## Key facts

- Distance and elevation: 226.9 km, 4,644 m D+ (altitude 515–1,383 m), a loop from and to Vitoria-Gasteiz.
- Areas: Entzia, Toloño, Cantabria and Izki ranges, Rioja Alavesa.
- Format: a single non-stop stage, true self-sufficiency, no assistance or classic aid stations. Official GPS track required and 6 stamping checkpoints.
- Time limit: 50 hours.
- Places: 300, in order of arrival of the pre-registration (a short personal description is mandatory). The pre-registration list opens on 1 December 2026; registrations open in January 2027.
- Zero Code: dropping a single piece of litter on the course means immediate disqualification.
- Safety: GPS tracker with SOS button and a control centre in Vitoria-Gasteiz.

# Ultra Trail Larre ®

A non-stop ultra-trail run in a single stage, fully self-supported , with no assistance and no classic aid stations, across the four Álavas: forest, vineyard, mountain range and plain.

226.9 KM Distance
4,644 D+ Elevation gain

Ultra Trail Larre® · Non-stop  ·  1st Edition · Autumn 2027

## One start.
One finish.
Nobody in between.

### The challenge

You set off at 16:00 from Parque de la Florida in Vitoria-Gasteiz and have 50 hours to come back to the same spot. What happens in between is yours to solve: food, water, sleep, the night and the way.
01
### Real self-sufficiency
No aid stations from the organisation and no outside assistance. You plan the race like an expedition, not like a circuit with a table every 15 km.

02
### Non-stop · 50 hours
The clock never stops. A single stage, two nights out on the terrain, and a control closing at 18:00, 50 hours after the start.

03
### You navigate
Official GPS track required, six checkpoints with a brevet card and a tracker with an SOS button. No ribbons every two hundred metres: here the route is read, not followed.

Forest Vineyard Mountains Plain

## Frequently asked questions

### FAQ

### When is it and where does it start?
The 1st edition of Ultra Trail Larre takes place in autumn 2027, with a single start at 16:00 from Parque de la Florida in Vitoria-Gasteiz, and finishes at the same spot. The exact date will be announced on this website and on @ultratraillarre.

### How long is the route?
Ultra Trail Larre is 226.9 km long with 4,644 m of positive elevation gain, a closed loop starting and finishing at Parque de la Florida, with a maximum time of 50 hours in a single stage. It is non-stop: the clock never stops, and stopping to sleep is a tactical decision for the runner.

### How do I get a place?
There are 300 places, allocated strictly in order of arrival of each pre-registration, which includes a mandatory short personal description; registrations open in January 2027. The pre-registration list opens on 1 December 2026. The description does not decide the place: order of arrival does.

### Are there aid stations?
There are no organiser aid stations and no outside assistance: each runner carries their own food and water, resupplies in the villages along the route and stamps a brevet card at six checkpoints. The only backup is a GPS tracker with an SOS button connected to the control centre.

### What is the Zero Code?
The Zero Code is the only rule with no exceptions: dropping a single piece of litter on the course means immediate disqualification and a ban from future editions, with no warning and no second chance. What goes into the mountains with the runner leaves the mountains with the runner.

### Is it a race?
There is a final ranking by order of arrival, but Ultra Trail Larre is conceived as a personal challenge, in the spirit of ultra-cycling and long self-supported routes, with no prizes for speed. For many, the challenge will simply be to finish.

# The 226.9 km
route

Ultra Trail Larre® is a non-stop ultra-trail: a single-stage loop that starts and finishes at Parque de la Florida in Vitoria-Gasteiz and crosses the four Álavas.

## Route data
Distance
226.9 km

Elevation gain
4,644 m

Altitude
515 m to 1,383 m (highest point at km 152.5)

Format
A single non-stop stage, loop

Start and finish
Parque de la Florida, Vitoria-Gasteiz

Start time
16:00

Time limit
50 hours (control closes at 18:00)

Areas
Entzia, Toloño, Cantabria and Izki ranges, and the Rioja Alavesa

Places
300 runners

Distance measured on the official track. Elevation gain is calculated from smoothed GPS altitude; unsmoothed, GPS noise would inflate it to nearly 5,000 m.

## Map and profile
Move the slider over the profile to follow the route kilometre by kilometre.

Highest point: 1,383 m · km 152.5

Official track · larre-2027.gpx · published 30 days before the start

## Stamping checkpoints
The route includes 6 stamping checkpoints. They are not aid stations: Ultra Trail Larre is run self-supported. Their locations will be confirmed before registrations open.

## Navigation
The official GPS track is mandatory. Every runner carries a GPS tracker with an SOS button, and the organisation runs a control centre in Vitoria-Gasteiz.
How to plan water, food, sleep and gear on a route like this is explained in the self-supported ultra guide .

# What is
Larre

Etymology, manifesto and the list of things we will never do.

## Etymology
larre [ ˈla.re ] · Basque · noun

In its most literal sense, larre names the upland meadow and pasture: open, uncultivated land where livestock graze freely. It also means open mountain and ground without marked paths, by extension any wild and rugged terrain, and, figuratively, what has not been tamed: what still belongs to everyone and to no one.

In a single syllable, the word holds the whole map of Álava: the beech forests of Izki Natural Park and the oak woods of Valderejo Natural Park; the terraced vineyards of the Rioja Alavesa below the Toloño range; the limestone ground and gorges of Okina; the cereal plain of the Llanada Alavesa; the high pastoral paths of the Entzia range; and the vast Ullíbarri-Gamboa reservoir, the territory's inner mirror.

The chosen noun evokes Álava's pastoral culture: transhumant flocks that for centuries stitched the four Álavas together in one seasonal movement, crossing forest, vineyard, mountain and plain. Larre is that same crossing, now on foot .

## Manifesto

We leave Vitoria-Gasteiz heading south and reach Peñacerrada-Urizaharra and the vineyards of Laguardia, beneath the Toloño range, facing the Ebro valley and the first lands of Rioja.

We cross the villages of the Rioja Alavesa, climb towards Santa Cruz de Campezo and up into the Entzia range, where the flocks of Álava's last transhumant shepherds still graze, before returning through Agurain to Vitoria-Gasteiz.

226.9 km that stitch the four Álavas into a single line.

Forest, vineyard, mountain and plain. Without assistance, without classic aid stations, without compulsory rest. With a GPS track, a brevet card and the certainty that the mountain is earned step by step .

- Total self-sufficiency

- No classic aid stations

- Zero waste in the mountains

- GPS tracker required

- Merged roadbook-brevet

- Mandatory gear checked

- Authored audiovisual production

- Small, demanding community

- Durable materials · no event kit

- Absolute respect for the territory

## Is it a race?
No.

Although some will treat it as one, Larre is a personal challenge . For many, the challenge will simply be to finish.

There will be a final ranking by order of arrival. But, following the traditions of ultra-cycling, bikepacking and long self-supported routes, there will be no prize for the fastest participant except the honour of arriving first.

No trophies are handed out here for speed. What is handed out is the privilege of having been there.

The culture of self-sufficiency understands that victory is not in beating the person next to you, but in holding your pace for 226.9 kilometres of mountain without anyone solving your water, your dinner or your sleep. That is the only competition that matters.

## Zero Code
The only trace we leave in the mountains is our footprints.
No wrappers, no stickers, no gels, no strips of tape. What goes into the mountains with the runner leaves the mountains with the runner.
It is not a slogan. It is a condition of entry. Every brevet card carries a zero-waste protocol signed at the briefing. Dropping a single piece of litter on the course, documented by photo, organiser, volunteer, another runner or scouting camera, means immediate disqualification and a ban from future editions . No nuances, no prior warning, no second chance.
That severity is deliberate. It is the only way to build a community that understands the privilege of being able to cross Toloño and Entzia. Most runners who already go self-supported live it that way naturally; we write it down so that nobody arrives without knowing.
The second axis is the durability of things. We produce few objects, make them to last for years, and design each one thinking of how it will be repaired before how it will be thrown away. The 1st Edition cap should still be in use in 2032. The brevet card is not paper: it is FSC card meant to be framed. The bib is technical fabric with reinforced stitching, not a piece of Tyvek that lasts a morning.
The most sustainable thing we produce is what we do not produce. Every year we review the whole pack and remove whatever adds nothing. We do not give things away for the sake of it. If a T-shirt is not the best T-shirt you will own this year, we do not give it to you.
The 10 rules of the Zero Code →

## We say NO long before we say YES
Almost everything that defines Larre is a list of things we will not do. Each NO on this page is a conscious decision: something the inertia of the trail-running market would push us to do and that we have ruled out as inconsistent with the project.
Saying NO is the only way to protect what matters. This list is neither exhaustive nor final: it grows every year as we learn what erodes the event and what sustains it.

- / 01
### No hot aid stations in the mountains
Self-sufficiency does not include a hot stew halfway round. Either you cook it yourself, or you buy it at a bar open to the public.

- / 02
### No inflatable start arch
PVC, generator, transport, waste. The start is where the runners are, not where the sponsored inflatable is.

- / 03
### No music or announcer at the start
This is not a village fair. The mountains do not need loudspeakers. The silence before the first step is part of the rite.

- / 04
### No plastic medals or heat-sealed screen printing
The finisher medal is solid recycled metal, die-cut by a supplier in the Basque Country. It is heavy, it lasts, it is handed down. It is not a badge.

- / 05
### No cash prize for the winner
There is no bonus for speed. Every finisher receives the same gift. The privilege of the first is being first, nothing more.

- / 06
### No polyester “free” T-shirt
Microplastic in the wash, thrown away in two years. The Larre shirt is certified organic cotton, a single design each edition. If you would not buy it, we do not give it to you.

- / 07
### No more places if “people are left out”
300 is 300. The 2nd Edition will be 300. The 10th Edition will be 300. The number is identity, not a market parameter. If you do not get in, you come back next year.

- / 08
### No barriers, carpet or red carpet in villages
We pass through villages that live all year round. A runner's passing should be visible but discreet. No ephemeral infrastructure in squares and streets.

This list will grow every year. If a decision we take today turns out to be inconsistent with the project, next year it joins the NO list and stays there. It is the only honest way to improve: documenting what we rule out, not just what we defend.

## Territory · zero impact, honestly
Larre's sustainability is not a badge on a website: it is a series of technical decisions at every stage of the project. No greenwashing and no green marketing: real, measured reduction and symbolic offsetting of the unavoidable through Retree the Planet.

- A
### Pack cut to 4 essentials
Cap and organic cotton T-shirt (single design per year · collectable), roadbook-brevet merged into FSC card, finisher medal in recycled metal. Technical bib separately as an operational item. No single-use plastics, no decorative merchandise.

- B
### Local production
Pack made in Álava where possible: local screen printing, sewing in workshops of the territory, and wines and preserves for the finish from producers within 30 km of the route.

- C
### Reusable trackers
GPS devices rented year after year, not consumables. Cases and straps reused. All the event's electronics are managed through rental, not purchase.

- D
### Clean mobility
Insistent communication to encourage train over car. Shared and, where possible, electric staff vehicles.

- E
### Carbon footprint
Annual calculation of the event's emissions (transport, production, staff accommodation) and offsetting through reforestation with Retree the Planet and local planting with HAZI / Provincial Council projects.

- F
### Durability above all
Every item in the pack is designed to last years, not hours. The cap should still be in use in 2032. The roadbook-brevet should be framed, not thrown away. The organic cotton T-shirt, a single design each edition, becomes a collector's item: whoever returns to Larre builds up a different piece every year. It is the antithesis of the event kit.

# The rules
of the game

The essentials of the 1st Edition rules, on one page.

## Essential rules
Format
A single non-stop stage of 226.9 km and 4,644 m D+.

Self-sufficiency
No assistance and no classic aid stations: each runner carries what they need.

Navigation
Official GPS track required, and stamping at the 6 checkpoints.

Time limit
50 hours from the start, with the control closing at 18:00.

Participation
300 places in order of arrival of the pre-registration, which includes a mandatory short personal description. Registrations in January 2027.

Safety
GPS tracker with SOS button, a control centre in Vitoria-Gasteiz and specific ultra-trail insurance covering rescue, helicopter included, and international civil liability.

Image rights
The runner grants image rights for editorial and promotional use of the event; direct commercial use requires individual written authorisation.

Mandatory gear
To be published with the final rules of the 1st Edition.

Summary of the essential rules of the 1st Edition published so far. Questions: ignacio@musubigara.org .
Download rules · PDF
What running self-supported involves is in the self-supported ultra guide . Pre-registration opens on 1 December 2026.

## Zero Code · 10 rules
Dropping a single piece of litter on the course means immediate disqualification and a ban from future editions. It is the only rule with no appeal.

- Zero waste in the mountains. All litter leaves in the runner's pack until the next inhabited place. Disqualification

- Reusable containers required. Flasks or soft flasks. Single-use bottles are banned from the starting kit. Disqualification

- Gels and bars: wrapper in your pack. Every wrapper that goes in must come out. Checked at the finish and at checkpoints. Disqualification

- No going off-track. You may not leave the route except on authorised diversions: not for a photo, a shortcut or a bivouac. Disqualification

- Bivouac without a trace. If you rest in the mountains, you leave no sign. No fires. No visible organic waste. Disqualification

- Reach the event by public transport. We promote train over car. Commitment

- Reusable pack, no single-use plastic. Organic cotton, FSC card, recycled technical fabric. No blister packs, no individual bags. Production

- Trackers on perpetual rental. The electronics fleet is rented year after year. We do not buy disposable GPS units. Straps and cases are reused. Production

- Finish-line food at km 0. At least 70% local produce from within 30 km of the route. No individual packaging. Production

- Annual public audit. The event's footprint (transport, production, logistics) is calculated and published. Real, measured reduction comes first, with symbolic offsetting of residual emissions through Retree the Planet. Transparency

# Get on
the list

300 places in order of arrival. Tell us who you are in a few lines: without a description the pre-registration is not validated, but it does not decide your place.

How it works: you fill in the form, you receive an email and confirm your address with a link (double confirmation). Order of arrival is set when you submit the form; only pre-registrations confirmed within 7 days count. Registrations open in January 2027.

# Getting to
the start

Ultra Trail Larre® starts and finishes in the same place: Parque de la Florida, in the centre of Vitoria-Gasteiz, capital of the Basque Country.

## Start and finish
Place
Parque de la Florida

City
Vitoria-Gasteiz, Álava (Basque Country)

Start
16:00 · autumn 2027 (1st Edition; the exact date will be announced later)

Finish
The same park, up to 50 hours after the start

See Parque de la Florida on Google Maps

## Getting to Vitoria-Gasteiz
By train or bus: the city has a railway station and a bus station, both a few minutes from the centre.
By plane: Vitoria-Gasteiz has its own airport (Foronda). Bilbao airport is a little over an hour away by road.
By car: the city is well connected by motorway with Bilbao, Donostia-San Sebastián, Pamplona and Burgos.
We promote train over car: it is one of the rules of the Zero Code .

## Logistics questions?
Write to ignacio@musubigara.org or on WhatsApp .

# Running
self-supported

What it means to run an ultra-trail without assistance, how much water and food you need, when to sleep and how to prepare for a 200 km distance.

## What a self-supported ultra-trail is

A self-supported ultra-trail is a race in which every runner carries everything they will need. There are no aid stations every fifteen kilometres, no drop bag, no crew car waiting at the top of the climb. There are checkpoints, yes, but they are control and stamping points: they confirm that you passed through, they do not feed you.

The difference from a classic ultra is not just logistics. It changes what you decide. In a supported ultra, the key decision is pace. In a self-supported one, the key decision is resource management: how much weight you carry, where you refill water, when you eat, when you sleep. Almost nobody drops out of a race like this for lack of legs; they drop out because they miscalculated the water, the food or the cold.

Aspect Supported ultra Self-supported

Aid stations Every 10–20 km None

Drop bag Common Does not exist

Outside assistance Allowed in marked zones Forbidden

Pack weight 1–3 kg 3–6 kg

Critical decision Pace Resources

## Water is the first problem

Water weighs a kilo per litre and you cannot carry all of it. So planning is done not by kilometres but by stretches between reliable water points: village fountains, bars, cemeteries, sports centres. They are marked on the map before the start, with an alternative in case one is dry or closed at night.

As a working reference, in mid-mountain terrain you drink around 400–500 ml per hour in mild temperatures and 600–800 ml per hour in the heat. Between two points five hours apart, that is more than two litres. A water filter or purification tablets weigh very little and turn any stream into an option; livestock troughs, no.

In autumn, in the Álava ranges, the trap is the opposite of what everyone expects: it is cool, you drink less than you think and you arrive dehydrated without ever having felt hot.

## Food: calculate by hours, not by kilometres

In long races most runners sustain between 200 and 300 kcal per hour, and almost never more. In an event that can last forty or fifty hours, that is many thousands of calories: more than fit in a reasonable pack. So the question is not “how much food do I carry” but “how much food do I carry on me and where does the rest come from”.

What works: alternating sweet and savoury before your stomach shuts down, combining solids with liquids, carrying something hot or salty for the small hours and having two or three options you know you can eat even when nauseous. What does not work: trying a gel, a bar or a flavour in the race that you have not tested on long training days.

Each race sets out in its rules whether you may buy in shops along the route or refill at public fountains, and that completely changes the food plan. It is the first thing to read. For Ultra Trail Larre the essentials are summarised in the rules .

## Sleeping, or not sleeping

An event with a fifty-hour time limit spans two nights. For most runners, not sleeping at all for forty-odd hours means reaching the second small hours with hallucinations, disorientation and bad decisions on terrain where decisions matter.

The three strategies actually used: not sleeping (only if you have already tried it in training and know how your head responds), micro-naps of ten to twenty minutes when the first serious low arrives, or a planned stop of one to two hours at a point decided in advance. The difference between it working and not working is having decided before the start, not at four in the morning lying in a ditch.

## The gear that really matters

Beyond what each organiser requires, there is a core that is not up for debate in self-supported racing:

- Headlamp with good battery life and a spare set of batteries or battery pack. Two nights are a lot of hours of light.

- Waterproof jacket with a hood and a dry thermal layer, kept for the night or for a stop.

- Charged phone, power bank and cables. It is your map, your emergency phone and your backup torch.

- Water capacity of 1.5–2 litres, plus a filter or tablets.

- Survival blanket and whistle. They weigh nothing and keep you alive while help arrives.

- Minimal foot kit: tape, small scissors, a needle, something for blisters. A badly treated blister retires more people than a climb.

- Gloves and a hat or neck gaiter. The cold at dawn on a ridge is nothing like the cold at the start.

The mandatory gear list for Ultra Trail Larre will be published with the final rules of the 1st Edition. When it is ready it will have its own page and will be announced on @ultratraillarre .

## Navigating with a GPS track

In self-supported races the route is not marked with ribbons: you follow an official GPS track. That means navigation is part of the event and is trained like a climb.

In practice: load the track on your watch and on your phone, with the area maps downloaded for use without coverage; mark the checkpoints as points of interest; know what to do when the watch warns you that you are off-track (stop, go back to the last safe point, do not improvise shortcuts at night); and do not depend on a single battery for the one thing that tells you where you are.

## Zero waste: how to run without leaving anything

At Ultra Trail Larre, dropping a single piece of litter means immediate disqualification, and it is the only rule in the regulations with no appeal. In practice it comes down to three habits: your own rubbish bag in a fixed pocket, always the same one; gels and bars with the tab tied or stowed the moment you open them, never “later”; and decanting what you can into reusable bags before the start, so you carry less wrapping from the beginning.

## How to prepare for a 200 km distance

With a year ahead, preparation falls into three blocks. This is not a personalised training plan (that depends on your history and, if there are health doubts, on a professional), but it is the structure shared by almost everyone who reaches the finish.

- Base · months 1 to 4 Accumulated volume and climbing, at a comfortable pace. Lots of time on your feet, little intensity. This builds the capacity to endure hours, not speed.

- Specific · months 5 to 8 Long back-to-back outings (Saturday and Sunday in a row), at least two complete night outings, all with the pack loaded to real race weight. You train your stomach by eating on the move what you will eat on race day.

- Sharpening · months 9 to 10 One long simulation of 12 to 24 hours with the final gear, the final food and footwear test, and then real rest. Whatever is not tested by now is not debuted in the race.

Two sessions are non-negotiable: running at night, for several hours, until not seeing clearly is normal; and chaining two long days in a row, to learn how the body responds when it starts with tired legs. And there are two parts that almost nobody trains and that decide races: the stomach and the feet.

## Ten mistakes that keep repeating

- Starting too fast in the first four hours because the pack does not weigh much yet.

- Debuting gear, footwear or nutrition on race day.

- Calculating water by kilometres rather than by time between reliable points.

- Having no sleep plan and deciding it in the small hours, with no judgement left.

- Carrying a single headlamp, or half-used spare batteries.

- Stopping eating as soon as nausea appears, instead of changing texture or flavour.

- Not treating the first discomfort in a foot to avoid losing ten minutes.

- Trusting a single battery for the GPS.

- Carrying the bare minimum of warm clothing because it was nice at the start.

- Not having read the rules until the week before.

## What this means at Ultra Trail Larre

Safety
GPS tracker with SOS button and a control centre in Vitoria-Gasteiz

The 16:00 start is not an aesthetic detail: you enter the night early, with fresh legs and almost the whole route ahead. Whoever has trained at night is grateful for it there. The full route is on the route page.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you run a 200 km ultra without having done a 100 first?

You can, but the chance of finishing drops a lot. What a 100 km or 24-hour event gives you is not the kilometres: it is having spent a night running, having handled a serious low and knowing what your stomach will eat at hour twenty. If there is no long ultra behind you, the reasonable substitute is your own outings of 15 to 24 hours on similar terrain.

### How much should the pack weigh?

In real self-sufficiency, between three and six kilos with water, depending on the weather and the sleep strategy. Below three usually means something important is missing; above six, that you are carrying fear in the form of weight.

### What happens if I decide to withdraw halfway?

In a self-supported race a withdrawal is always reported to the organisation; nobody drops out silently: until they know, the control centre assumes you are still in the mountains. The specific Ultra Trail Larre procedure (pick-up points and phone number) will be part of the final rules and of the compulsory briefing the day before.

### Is Ultra Trail Larre a good first self-supported race?

Honestly, no. It is a good second or third step. To start in the format, a 50 to 100 km event with no assistance, or your own two-day route, makes more sense. What Ultra Trail Larre is, is a place where self-sufficiency is not decoration on the poster: 226.9 km, zero waste and a track with you, the mountain and your brevet.

## The places

The 1st Edition has 300 bibs, allocated in order of arrival of the pre-registration, which includes a mandatory short personal description. Registrations open in January 2027. If you want us to let you know on day one, leave your details on the pre-registration list .

# Privacy
policy

What data we collect when you pre-register, what for, for how long and what rights you have. Version 2026-11-v1.

## 1. Data controller

- Controller: Ignacio Sanz Arana

- Tax ID (NIF): 72752567-W

- Postal address: Pablo Uranga 10, 01008 Vitoria-Gasteiz (Álava), Spain

- Contact: ignacio@musubigara.org

## 2. Data we process

- Pre-registration form data: full name, email, country of residence, personal description, experience (optional), language, and your choice about receiving news.

- Record data: date and time of submission and confirmation, order number, version of the consent text you accepted.

- Technical data: IP address and browser, which the form provider logs on submission for security and anti-spam reasons.
We do not ask for special categories of data. Please do not include them in your description.

## 3. Purposes and legal basis

- Managing your pre-registration: validating your email (double confirmation), assigning the order-of-arrival number and contacting you about the opening of registrations. Basis: your consent (art. 6.1.a GDPR) and pre-contractual measures at your request (art. 6.1.b).

- Sending you Ultra Trail Larre® news , only if you tick the optional box. Basis: your consent (art. 6.1.a). You can withdraw it at any time without affecting the above.

- Security and prevention of form abuse. Basis: legitimate interest (art. 6.1.f).
No automated decisions or profiling take place. The personal description is mandatory but does not determine your place: that is set by the order of arrival of confirmed pre-registrations.

## 4. Retention periods

- Unconfirmed pre-registrations: deleted after 30 days.

- Confirmed pre-registrations: until the 1st Edition registration process ends; they are then deleted, unless you register, in which case the registration conditions apply.

- News subscription: until you unsubscribe.

- Data may be kept blocked for the limitation periods of possible legal liabilities.

## 5. Recipients and processors
We do not disclose your data to third parties except where legally required. To provide the service we use the following processors, with whom the corresponding data processing agreement (art. 28 GDPR) is in place:

- Netlify, Inc. : website hosting, form collection and running the functions that handle pre-registration.

- Resend, Inc. : sending the confirmation email.

## 6. International transfers
Both providers are established in the United States. Transfers rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework where the provider is certified and, failing that, on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses. You may ask us for more information about the safeguards applied.

## 7. Your rights
You may exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction of processing and portability, and withdraw your consent, by writing to ignacio@musubigara.org and stating the email you pre-registered with. We will reply within one month.
If you believe we have not processed your data in line with the rules, you may lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency ( www.aepd.es ).

## 8. Cookies and tracking
This site uses no first-party or third-party cookies, and no analytics or advertising tools. Fonts are served from the site itself.

## 9. Security
We apply reasonable technical and organisational measures: encrypted connection (HTTPS), signed confirmation links with an expiry, restricted access to data and periodic deletion of unconfirmed data.

## 10. Changes
If this policy changes materially, a new version and date will be published here. The version of the text you accept is recorded with your pre-registration.
